blocks.html: Bulk SMS vs WhatsApp marketing is not a contest with one winner: SMS reaches every phone, WhatsApp lets you show and say more, and the right choice depends on the message, the customer and the rules each channel follows. Most businesses end up using both, with a clear rule for which message goes where.

This guide compares the two channels on reach, consent, approvals, format, billing basis, delivery proof and risk, then maps common messages to the right channel, and shows how to combine them. sections.heading: Bulk SMS vs WhatsApp Marketing: The Short Answer

blocks.html: Use SMS for reach and simple alerts, WhatsApp for richer, opted-in conversations, and both together when you can. Here is the quick comparison.

items.title: SMS strength:
items.desc: reaches any phone with network coverage, with no app and no data connection.

items.title: WhatsApp strength:
items.desc: images, buttons and two-way chat for customers who have opted in.

items.title: Approvals:
items.desc: SMS needs TRAI DLT. WhatsApp needs Meta template approval. Neither is approval-free.

items.title: Consent:
items.desc: WhatsApp requires opt-in before you message first. Promotional SMS has DND and timing rules.

items.title: Billing:
items.desc: SMS is priced per message by your provider. WhatsApp is billed by Meta per delivered template, by category and country.

items.title: Best together:
items.desc: WhatsApp first for opted-in customers, with SMS as the fallback.

sections.heading: Bulk SMS vs WhatsApp Marketing: Side by Side

blocks.html: Compare them one dimension at a time. Each difference changes which messages suit which channel.

items.title: Reach:
items.desc: SMS reaches any phone with coverage. WhatsApp reaches people who have WhatsApp and a data connection.

items.title: Consent:
items.desc: WhatsApp requires opt-in before a business messages first. Promotional SMS must respect DND and the 9 AM to 9 PM window.

items.title: Approvals:
items.desc: SMS: DLT entity, sender ID and template. WhatsApp: Meta template approval and a verified business account.

items.title: Format:
items.desc: SMS is plain text. WhatsApp supports images, documents, buttons and interactive messages.

items.title: Two-way chat:
items.desc: WhatsApp supports a conversation. SMS replies are limited and harder to manage.

items.title: Delivery proof:
items.desc: SMS gives a delivery report. WhatsApp reports sent, delivered and read status for each message.

items.title: Billing basis:
items.desc: SMS is a per-message rate set by your provider. WhatsApp is billed by Meta per delivered template, by category and country.

items.title: Main risk:
items.desc: SMS: template and category rejections, DND blocks. WhatsApp: low quality, blocks and reports, and policy violations.

sections.heading: Compliance: TRAI DLT for SMS, Meta Rules for WhatsApp

blocks.html: Each channel has its own rulebook, and they do not overlap. Knowing which applies saves you from rejected templates and blocked messages.

items.title: SMS: TRAI and DLT:
items.desc: register your entity, sender ID and each template, and send only text that matches the approved template. See our guide to DLT registration charges in India.

items.title: SMS: DND and timing:
items.desc: promotional SMS cannot reach DND numbers and is limited to the 9 AM to 9 PM window, while transactional messages such as OTPs can reach DND numbers.

items.title: WhatsApp: Meta policy:
items.desc: you may message only people who opted in, and you must start conversations with approved templates. Read the WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy.

items.title: WhatsApp: use the official platform:
items.desc: WhatsApp's FAQ says its apps are not intended for bulk or automated messaging. See how to send bulk WhatsApp messages safely.

items.title: Both: DPDP Act:
items.desc: treat mobile numbers as personal data, collected for a clear purpose, with easy withdrawal.

blocks.html: This is practical guidance rather than legal advice, so check your own obligations with a qualified professional.

sections.heading: How Each Channel Bills: Compare Without the Guesswork

blocks.html: Headline rupee figures for these channels vary widely between websites, and many are out of date, because Meta changed how WhatsApp is billed in July 2025. We do not quote rates here. Instead, compare how each channel bills and ask for itemised quotes.

items.title: SMS:
items.desc: your provider sets a per-message rate, based on route, category and volume. Regional-language messages can use more than one segment.

items.title: WhatsApp:

items.title: Cost per outcome:
items.desc: compare orders, bookings or replies per rupee spent, not the price of a single message.

items.title: Provider charges:
items.desc: ask both providers whether platform fees, onboarding, support and reports are included, and whether quotes include GST.

sections.heading: Who Should Start With Which Channel

blocks.html: Your audience should decide where you start. Use what you know about their phones, their data and their habits.

items.title: Feature-phone or low-data customers:
items.desc: start with SMS, because WhatsApp cannot reach them reliably.

items.title: Smartphone-first customers, such as D2C shoppers:
items.desc: start with WhatsApp for opted-in customers, with SMS fallback.

items.title: Dealers, distributors and B2B contacts:
items.desc: WhatsApp for order and payment updates once they opt in, SMS for critical alerts.

items.title: Regulated or audit-heavy messages:
items.desc: keep SMS as the guaranteed path, and check your regulator's and partners' requirements.

items.title: Regional-language audiences:
items.desc: both channels support regional languages, but SMS needs Unicode and a registered template in that script.

blocks.html: Do not trust headline numbers from other websites. Test on your own customers and compare cost per outcome.

items.title: Use comparable audiences:
items.desc: split similar customers between the two channels, with the same offer.

items.title: Track the full funnel:

items.title: Treating them as interchangeable:

items.q: Is bulk SMS or WhatsApp marketing better for my business?
items.a: Neither wins on every measure. SMS reaches any phone with network coverage, with no app or data needed, while WhatsApp supports images, buttons and two-way chat for customers who have opted in. Match the channel to the message and the customer, and consider using both with SMS as the fallback.

items.q: Can I use bulk SMS and WhatsApp marketing together?
items.a: Yes, and many businesses do. A common setup is WhatsApp first for opted-in smartphone customers, with SMS as the fallback for customers who are not on WhatsApp or whose message was not delivered. Running both through one provider keeps consent records, reports and fallback in one place.

items.q: Does WhatsApp marketing need DLT registration?
items.a: No. DLT registration under TRAI's rules applies to SMS. WhatsApp follows Meta's template approval and opt-in policies. If you add an SMS fallback, that SMS still needs your DLT entity, sender ID and approved template.

items.q: Can WhatsApp marketing reach DND numbers?
items.a: DND is a telecom registry that applies to SMS, and promotional SMS cannot reach DND-registered numbers. WhatsApp has no DND registry, but it has its own rule: you may message only people who opted in to hear from you. A customer on DND can still receive WhatsApp messages if they opted in.

items.q: Which channel is better for OTPs?
items.a: Use SMS as the baseline, because it reaches any phone. WhatsApp OTPs can be faster to complete for users on WhatsApp with data, with copy-code and autofill buttons. A WhatsApp-first flow with SMS fallback suits many startups. Our guide on WhatsApp OTP vs SMS OTP compares them in detail.

items.q: How do I compare SMS and WhatsApp results fairly?
items.a: Send the same offer to comparable audiences, then compare cost per outcome, such as orders or bookings, not cost per message. Track delivery, taps or replies, conversions and opt-outs. Avoid trusting headline statistics from other sites, and benchmark your own customers.

items.q: Is WhatsApp marketing legal in India?
items.a: Sending through the official WhatsApp Business Platform to customers who opted in is permitted by WhatsApp's policy. You must also follow Indian law, including the principles of the DPDP Act. WhatsApp's own FAQ says its apps are not meant for bulk or automated messaging, so use the official API. This is practical guidance rather than legal advice.

items.q: When should a business choose SMS over WhatsApp?
items.a: Choose SMS when your audience includes feature-phone users or people with little data, when you need to reach customers who have not opted in on WhatsApp through compliant SMS, or when the message is a simple alert such as an OTP or order confirmation. SMS also works as the universal fallback.
